ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The quarter’s missed volume is concentrated in the two non-brand search campaigns, and the limiting factor is predominantly rank rather than budget. Both Non-Brand Search - Flights and Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages run at only 33–35% search impression share while losing ~51% to rank (vs only 14–16% to budget) and still show meaningful budget headroom (budget utilization 61.4–63.6%). Within those campaigns there are several high-quality keywords stuck at ~30–36% impression share with 64–70% lost to rank, indicating bids/ad rank (and for Hotels & Packages also quality score) is holding back, not daily budget caps.
notable_patterns: Non-Brand Search - Flights: 33% search impression share with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, while budget utilization is only 63.6%—demand exists but ad rank is the bigger limiter.

Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages: 35% search impression share with 51% lost to rank vs 14% lost to budget, and the campaign’s avg quality score is only 5.1 (lowest in the account), suggesting quality is a material driver of rank loss here.

High-quality keywords are still rank-limited: e.g., “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) at 34% impression share with 66% lost to rank; “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) at 30% IS with 70% lost to rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) at 36% IS with 64% lost to rank.

Query mix is diluted by competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ exposure: 10,640 impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms, representing 48.5% of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms, yet only one competitor term is shown converting (“trailmark travel quote” at 0.5 conversions).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Volume is materially constrained by rank: search impression share is 33% with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, and budgets are not being fully utilized (63.6%). Keyword evidence shows multiple strong-QS flight terms still losing 66–70% impression share to rank (e.g., “flights to spain” QS 8.5; “cheap flights europe” QS 7.5).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase ad rank on proven high-intent flight terms (bid/target adjustments and tightening query match intent), while cutting or isolating low-intent service queries (e.g., “flight booking customer service” QS 4.0; £372.28 spend; £195.94/conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is also rank-limited (35% impression share; 51% lost to rank vs 14% budget) and has the weakest average quality score in the account (5.1), which is consistent with rank loss. There’s also measurable self-blocking via negatives ("visa" blocking “weekend city breaks visa requirements”, ~1,150 estimated blocked impressions).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize quality score and ad rank improvements on top hotel/package themes, resolve the “visa” negative conflict, and reduce spend on low-intent policy queries (e.g., “hotel cancellation policy” QS 4.5; £279.27 spend; £116.36/conv).

recommendation_cards.title: Push ad rank on high-QS non-brand winners (don’t let 64–70% rank loss persist)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across the two in-scope campaigns, rank loss is the dominant limiter (both at 51% impression share lost to rank vs only 14–16% lost to budget, with budget utilization still only 61.4–63.6%). Even high-quality keywords are stuck at low impression share due to rank: “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) is 30% IS with 70% lost to rank; “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) is 34% IS with 66% lost to rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) is 36% IS with 64% lost to rank.
recommended_steps: Segment these high-QS, high-intent terms into their own tightly themed ad groups (or a dedicated campaign) so bid/target changes apply cleanly and aren’t diluted by mixed intent.
Increase bids/targets specifically on these segments until impression share lost to rank meaningfully falls (start with the worst offenders: 66–70% lost to rank).
Use a controlled holdout (one theme unchanged) to confirm incremental conversions/ROAS rather than just paying more for the same clicks.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to rank on the carved-out high-intent segments dropping from ~64–70% toward <45%, while maintaining non-brand ROAS near current levels (Flights 9.68; Hotels & Packages 11.57).

recommendation_cards.title: Fix Hotels & Packages quality score drag (avg QS 5.1) to recover rank without proportional CPC inflation
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages has the lowest avg quality score in the account (5.1) and simultaneously loses 51% impression share to rank at only 35% impression share overall. Keyword-level evidence indicates quality score is strongly tied to impression share (r=0.957) and inversely tied to cost per conversion (r=-0.883), so improving QS here should both regain rank and protect efficiency.
recommended_steps: Rewrite/refresh ads and landing alignment for the top hotel/package themes (e.g., mirror ‘all inclusive holidays’ and ‘weekend city breaks’ language in headlines and on the landing page above the fold) to lift expected CTR and relevance.
Split out policy/info intent into separate ad groups (or exclude it) so primary booking-intent groups maintain stronger CTR and relevance signals.

Audit the weakest-QS, highest-cost queries/keywords in this campaign first (e.g., “hotel cancellation policy” QS 4.5; £279.27 spend; £116.36/conv) and either exclude, downbid, or move to a support-only structure with capped bids.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Average quality score in Hotels & Packages moving from 5.1 toward 6.0+, alongside a reduction in campaign-level impression share lost to rank from 51% toward <45%.

recommendation_cards.title: Reduce wasted competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ exposure that’s crowding query mix
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Search-term logs show 10,640 impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms, and 48.5% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms. Conversions from competitor terms are negligible in the evidence provided (only “trailmark travel quote” shows 0.5 conversions), suggesting a large share of this exposure is not yielding site engagement.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names from the zero-click list (e.g., “skyline journeys”, “coastal getaways”, “horizon holidays”) as negatives in non-brand campaigns where they are triggering, while optionally whitelisting the one shown converting term pattern around “trailmark travel quote”.
Re-check the search-term feed after 3–7 days to confirm competitor-brand impression volume drops materially without hurting non-brand conversions.
If competitor conquesting is a deliberate strategy, isolate it into a separate campaign with its own budget/targets so it can’t dilute core non-brand ranking efforts.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Competitor-brand zero-click impressions falling from 10,640 and the share of impressions from zero-click competitor terms dropping from 48.5% toward <20%.

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve self-blocking negatives that are suppressing demand (1,790 blocked impressions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 2 conflicts blocking an estimated 1,790 impressions: negative “visa” blocks “weekend city breaks visa requirements” in Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages (~1,150 impressions), and negative “jobs” blocks “flight attendant jobs cheap flights europe” in Non-Brand Search - Flights (~640 impressions).
recommended_steps: Replace broad negatives with more precise variants (e.g., keep excluding employment intent with targeted ‘recruitment/careers/salary’ negatives rather than blocking mixed queries that include core travel terms).
Use campaign-level negative scoping so exclusions meant for one theme (employment/info) don’t suppress booking-intent ad groups.
After changes, verify the blocked keywords can receive impressions again and confirm the traffic is actually relevant (and re-add tighter negatives if it’s not).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions from conflicts trending from 1,790 toward ~0, and impression share on affected themes increasing without a spike in irrelevant search terms.

already_working: Brand Search - UK efficiency is very strong (ROAS 48.18 on £9,631.08 spend) and budget is not the primary limiter (only 58.5% budget utilization; 10% lost to budget vs 20% to rank).
Ad coverage/asset quality is largely in good shape: 83.3% of ads are rated Excellent or Good (4 Excellent, 1 Good out of 6).

Auction position is generally competitive: self top-of-page rate averages 66.3% vs competitor 53.9%, and self outranking share is 61.4%, suggesting the biggest gains are more about targeted rank recovery on specific non-brand themes than an account-wide competitiveness crisis.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Non-brand volume is being missed primarily because ad rank is suppressing impression share—not because budgets are capped—at the same moment the market is showing sharp QoQ growth in both travel query demand and search spend. With competitors also holding meaningful spend share in search (and broader multi-channel pressure), delaying rank/quality-score fixes risks locking in a structurally lower share-of-voice during a rising-demand quarter, especially on fast-growing flight themes like “flights to spain.”

supporting_facts.fact: Travel (United Kingdom) shows +19.0% Query Demand Growth QoQ and +22.0% Spend Growth QoQ, with Vertical-Avg Impression Share at 40.0% (Table: “Vertical | Highlighted Market | Spend Growth QoQ | Query Demand Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share”, p.5).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Demand and competitive spend are rising at the same time; because the account’s non-brand campaigns are rank-constrained, improving ad rank now is the fastest way to capture incremental impressions/clicks while the market is expanding.

supporting_facts.fact: United Kingdom (pilot account market) Search Spend Growth QoQ is 22.0% and Vertical-Avg Impression Share is 40.0% (Table: “Market | Search Spend Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share”, p.13).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A +22% QoQ increase in search spend signals intensifying auctions; if rank loss persists, the account will continue to under-deliver on impressions even with budget headroom, making near-term bid/ad-rank action time-sensitive.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword “flights to spain” index grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 151 (Q3 2026), for 51% growth (Table: “Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This directly matches one of the account’s highlighted high-QS but rank-limited keywords; with the query growing +51%, fixing rank loss now prevents the account from missing a rapidly expanding pool of high-intent searches.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword “budget airline flight deals” index grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 141 (Q3 2026), for 41% growth (Table: “Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth”, p.11).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports urgency to raise rank/coverage on flight-deal intent (a core non-brand theme) because query volume is expanding materially; delaying rank improvements likely forfeits incremental conversions during a growth period.

supporting_facts.fact: Skyline Journeys holds 22% Spend Share and is active on “Search, Video” (Table: “Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A major competitor with 22% spend share and search presence increases auction pressure; when the account is losing impressions to rank (not budget), prompt ad-rank improvements are needed to defend and grow non-brand visibility.

supporting_facts.fact: Coastal Getaways holds 18% Spend Share and runs “Search, Social” (Table: “Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Another large spender active in search reinforces that non-brand auctions are contested; improving rank (and Hotels & Packages quality score) now helps avoid being out-positioned as competitors maintain heavy investment.

supporting_facts.fact: Horizon Holidays holds 16% Spend Share with 34 Active Creatives across “Search, Social, Video” (Table: “Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: High creative volume across channels suggests strong competitive pressure and message testing; rank-constrained campaigns should act now (bids/RSAs/landing alignment) to avoid continued impression loss while competitors iterate.

supporting_facts.fact: Pilot Account (this report) is shown with 14.0% Spend Share and channel focus “Search (primary)” (Table: “Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: With search as the primary channel and a defined spend share in the competitive set, capturing more impression share depends heavily on ad rank/quality improvements; it’s a near-term lever with immediate reach impact in the core channel.

email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 sits behind rank loss (47.0%), not budget
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t “tapping out” on budget right now — it’s getting boxed out on position. With a GBP 6,200 daily budget in place, the non-brand campaigns are still leaving a lot of qualified demand on the table simply because ads aren’t showing often enough when intent is strongest.
why_now_bullets: Non-brand coverage is being throttled by rank: **47.0% lost to rank** vs **15.2% lost to budget** (overall impression share sits at **37.84%**).
The market’s accelerating at the same time: UK travel is **+19.0% Query Demand Growth QoQ** alongside **+22.0% Spend Growth QoQ** — auctions get harder while demand gets more valuable.
One of your strongest flight themes is spiking: “flights to spain” shows **51% growth** (index 100 -> 151), and your current rank loss means you’re under-exposed right as that query pool expands.
email_copy.stat_sub: Rank-constrained non-brand is the bottleneck — not daily caps
email_copy.impact_line: We sized GBP 316,559 in incremental revenue opportunity this quarter by recovering missed non-brand visibility that’s currently being lost to rank, even though budgets aren’t fully doing the limiting. In other words: you don’t need to “spend more everywhere” — you need to win more of the right auctions on the queries you already know can perform.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is where that missed volume is concentrated, by campaign, so you can see exactly which parts of non-brand are being held back.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the short list of fixes that should unlock share-of-voice fastest: targeted rank lift on proven winners, quality-score cleanup where it’s dragging position, and removing query waste that’s diluting the signal.
email_copy.working_intro: Also worth calling out: several fundamentals are already solid — which is why this looks like a focused rank recovery problem, not a rebuild.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we execute the rank + query-mix cleanups, the payoff is straightforward: moving impression share from **37.84%** toward **40.0%** is what drives the additional reach/click volume shown below — and it’s the cleanest path to capturing that GBP 316,559 this quarter.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map the first 7 days of changes?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with either “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send a tight 7-day action plan (what we change first, what we hold out for proof, and what success looks like). If easier, just reply “plan” and I’ll email it over async.
email_copy.ps: P.S. The goal isn’t higher CPCs — it’s selectively buying back rank where you’re already strong, while trimming the queries that are soaking up attention without producing bookings.
